'''Landon Curt Noll''' (born October 28, 1960)<ref>[http://www.paulnoll.com/Oregon/Sons/Landon-at-birth.html Paul Noll's article on the birth of his son, Landon]</ref><ref>[http://home.comcast.net/~igpl/NWS.html Naming Large Numbers]</ref> is an American [[computer scientist]], co-discoverer of the 25th [[Mersenne prime]] and discoverer of the 26th,<ref>Noll C, Nickel L: The 25th and 26th Mersenne Primes, ''[[Mathematics of Computation]]'' '''35''': 1387-1390, {{doi|10.2307/2006405}}</ref> which he found while still enrolled at [[Hayward High School (California)|Hayward High School]] and concurrently at [[California State University, East Bay|California State University, Hayward]].<ref>[http://primes.utm.edu/bios/page.php?id=30 The Prime Pages bio for Landon Curt Noll]</ref>

==Biography==
Noll was born in [[Walnut Creek, California]], [[United States]].  At age 18, he became the youngest person to break the record for the [[largest known prime]].  He has held or co-held the record three times.<ref>[http://primes.utm.edu/notes/by_year.html#table2 Records by Electronic Computer]</ref>
He is also the co-inventor (with [[John Horton Conway]]) of a system for naming arbitrarily large powers of 10.<ref>[http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/math/number/howhigh.html How high can you count?]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.isthe.com/cgi-bin/number.cgi |title=The English name of a number |access-date=2007-10-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060519000731/http://www.isthe.com/cgi-bin/number.cgi |archive-date=2006-05-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
He also helped start the [[International Obfuscated C Code Contest]],<ref>[http://www.ioccc.org/faq.html Frequently Asked Questions about the International Obfuscated C Code Contest]</ref> and is a co-inventor of the [[Fowler Noll Vo hash]] function.<ref>[http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/comp/fnv/index.html#history Fowler/Noll/Vo (FNV) hash history]</ref>

He was also a member of the [[Amdahl Six]]<ref>[http://primes.utm.edu/bios/code.php?code=Z  The Prime Pages bio for the Amdahl Six]</ref> team (John S. Brown, Bodo Parady, Curt Landon Noll, Gene W. Smith, Joel F. Smith, and Sergio E. Zarantonello) which discovered another record prime in 1989; this prime remains unusual as a record large prime as it was not a Mersenne prime.<ref>[http://perso.orange.fr/yves.gallot/primes/index.html Generalized Fermat Prime Search]</ref><ref>[http://primes.utm.edu/bios/page.php?id=753  Yves Gallot's GFN Search Project]</ref>

Noll is an amateur astronomer.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://members.aas.org/directory/memberdetails.cfm?Par=27859 |title=American Astronomical Society for Landon Curt Noll |access-date=2007-10-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070326062000/http://members.aas.org/directory/memberdetails.cfm?Par=27859 |archive-date=2007-03-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/astro/index.html Landon Curt Noll's Astronomy pages].</ref> His work includes measuring the [[Solar parallax]] during the 2004 [[Transit of Venus]]<ref>[http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/astro/venus2004.html Transit of Venus 8 June 2004]</ref> as well as the search for [[Vulcanoid asteroid]]s.<ref>[http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/astro/index.html Reference to "The search for Vulcanoid asteroids, Sky and Telescope, Jan 2006, Pages 87-89]</ref>

He was also involved in politics as a [[Sunnyvale, California]] city council member and vice-mayor.<ref>{{cite web |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100223105320/http://sunnyvale.ca.gov/council-minutes/1996/minutes11-19-96.htm |archivedate=23 February 2010 |url=http://sunnyvale.ca.gov/council-minutes/1996/minutes11-19-96.htm |title=Minutes, Sunnyvale City Council, 19 November 1996}}</ref>
